questions.prompt: Training MSE as a function of polynomial degree for fixed data (least squares) is:
options: Non-increasing, because the models are nested
Decreasing then increasing like test error
questions.explanation: A higher-degree family contains the lower one, so its best training fit is at least as good.

questions.prompt: Collecting 10 times more data helps most when the learning curves show:
options: A large gap that shrinks as n grows (high variance)
Converging high errors on both curves (high bias)
Zero training error and zero test error already
A test error that is already below the noise floor
questions.explanation: More data reduces variance, not bias.

questions.prompt: A cubic fitted on x in [-1, 0.5] is evaluated on x in [0.5, 1]. What is expected?
options: Lower error, because the function is flatter out there
Undefined, because the fit refuses to run outside the range
The same error, since the function is smooth everywhere
Much larger error than on the training range (extrapolation)
questions.explanation: Polynomials extrapolate poorly; this is covariate shift. In the lesson the MSE grew from 0.095 to 0.687.

questions.prompt: In ridge regression, increasing lambda from 0 to a large value has what effect?
questions.explanation: Coefficients are shrunk toward zero: more bias, less variance.

questions.prompt: Noise standard deviation is 0.5, and a model has test MSE 0.40. What is the maximum possible improvement (reducible error)? Give a number with 2 decimals.

Prediction errors at one input from four models are summarized by predictions 0.7, 1.1, 0.9, 1.3 with true value 1.0. What is the variance of the predictions (population variance, divide by 4)? Give a number with 2 decimals.
A test accuracy of 0.85 is measured on 400 independent test items. What is the half-width of the 95% confidence interval (1.96 standard errors)? Give a number with 3 decimals.
103 samples, 10-fold CV with fold sizes as equal as possible. How many folds have 11 samples? Integer.
questions.explanation: 103 = 10*10 + 3, so 3 folds have 11 samples and 7 have 10.

questions.prompt: Explain how to estimate the generalization error of a model whose hyperparameter lambda is tuned by cross-validation, without optimistic bias.
rubric: Hold out a test set before tuning and touch it once at the end, or use nested cross-validation.
Tune lambda (and all preprocessing) using only training folds.
Notes that the best CV score is optimistic because it was selected.

rubric: High variance (large initial gap) that is closing with more data.
Action: gather more data and/or add regularization or simplify the model.

rubric: Split indices into k folds first.
